subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should CLI health/status/config-preflight paths become RPC/read-only while a local gateway owns state/openclaw.sqlite, and what fail-closed or doctor/quarantine recovery should apply when the DB is already malformed?
rationale: Source confirms non-gateway CLI paths can still open and checkpoint the shared DB; the right fix changes state ownership, direct-file fallback behavior, and recovery policy rather than one isolated call site.

options.title: RPC/read-only owner boundary
options.body: Make health/status prefer gateway RPC and ensure any direct DB fallback opens without WAL maintenance, schema migrations, writes, or checkpoints while the gateway is live.

options.title: Exclusive gateway lease
options.body: Have the gateway own read-write state access and make CLI direct DB access fail closed with a clear doctor/RPC path while that lease is held.

options.title: Recovery-only hardening
options.body: Keep current opener behavior but add malformed-DB quarantine and doctor repair, which reduces damage after corruption but leaves the suspected trigger path in place.

recommendation.title: RPC/read-only owner boundary
recommendation.body: Make health/status prefer gateway RPC and ensure any direct DB fallback opens without WAL maintenance, schema migrations, writes, or checkpoints while the gateway is live.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the shared SQLite state base and plugin index migration ownership that define the affected boundary.
